purpose: The design and content-production suggestion layer: a paste-ready design prompt, design suggestions with live status, the article topic queue with published/pending status, organic-traffic tactics, editorial voice rules, and a decision register. Every row is a suggestion for the owner to review before anything is implemented. Facts about the current site carry source links; everything else is a recommendation, not a claim.
how_to_read: Status values describe the repository as built on 2026-11-15 and are checked against the files themselves: 'Implemented' means the generated pages already do this; 'Partial' means it exists but a named part is missing; 'Pending' means it has not been started. Decision rows are left blank on purpose — this page exists so a path can be chosen before work begins.
design_prompt:
ZONE1 KITCHEN — DESIGN PROMPT (paste-ready)
Goal: polish this Amazon affiliate site so it reads like a human-run marketing publication — not an AI-generated data dump — without weakening its verification discipline.

SITE AS IT IS TODAY (do not contradict these facts)
- Static site generated by build.py from data/*.json; live at https://kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone1/
- Three tracked air fryers (Chefman 6 Qt dual-basket, Emeril 26 QT French-door oven, Chefman 8 Qt single-basket). The supplied Amazon short links resolve to candidate ASINs whose product identity is UNCONFIRMED and must stay labelled as such.
- Every published number carries a source badge (S1-S31) linking to the official page it came from. Values that cannot be confirmed are left blank and listed on the Flagged-for-review page — never guessed, never back-filled.
- Amazon prices, star ratings and review counts are NEVER displayed (Amazon Program Policies 2(b) and 6(t)). Manufacturer list prices are allowed when cited to the brand's own page.
- No hands-on testing is ever claimed; no superlative ("best", "top-rated") is asserted as fact; vendor statements are labelled as brand claims.
- An affiliate disclosure bar sits above the header on every page: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."

DESIGN DIRECTION
1. Keep the dashboard skeleton — sticky sidebar, top bar, disclosure band, stat tiles, sourced tables — and keep the landing page editorial: one-sentence value proposition above the fold, then a format finder, then sourced article cards.
2. Palette: warm off-white #f6f7f9, ink #111827, brand teal #0f766e with soft aqua #ccfbf1, amber accent #ca784d; warn/bad/ok states already exist as CSS variables — reuse them, do not invent new colors.
3. Typography: system sans for UI, serif display for hero headlines (--serif is already in use). Sentence case; tight letter-spacing on display sizes.
4. Components that must survive any redesign: source badge (S#), blank cell with "not confirmed" pill, flag pill, stat tile, callout variants (info/warn/bad), comparison table with per-cell source links, disclosure bar.
5. Mobile-first: single column below 820px, tap targets at least 40px, no horizontal scroll, prefers-reduced-motion respected, focus-visible outlines kept.
6. Page inventory to keep: Home, This week's picks, Buying guide, Articles, Category, three product pages, Comparison, Full dataset, Compliance, Flagged, Suggestions, Questions, Decisions & handover, Executive summary, Re-verification, Platform, Previous passes, Design prompt pack.

EDITORIAL VOICE (anti-AI-slop rules - non-negotiable)
- No unverified superlatives: never "best", "top-rated", "revolutionary", "must-have", "game-changing". If it is not sourced, do not say it.
- Specific numbers beat intensifiers. Contractions and questions are welcome. Mix short and long sentences.
- Show the gaps: blank cells, published conflicts and "unconfirmed" badges are content, not bugs.
- Label every manufacturer statement as a brand claim, not a tested fact.
- Never write "we tested", "our pick", "in our kitchen". The site does not test products.
- One topic per page; every page stamps when its sources were read.
- Banned openers and claim guards are enforced in build.py (see decisions.html, anti-slop list).

SEO LAYER (already implemented - keep it)
- Every page carries canonical URL, og:* tags, twitter:card, meta description and JSON-LD (WebSite / Article / BreadcrumbList); robots.txt and sitemap.xml are regenerated by build.py; a build guard (check_seo_metadata) fails the build if any of it is dropped. Social card: assets/og-card.png.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (all must pass before any change merges)
1. python3 build.py — all build guards green: every table row sourced, disclosure present, SEO metadata present, affiliate links qualified rel=sponsored, no price/rating leakage, unique flag IDs.
2. python3 verify.py — 0 errors.
3. bash scripts/ci-check.sh — unit tests, data audit, link check all green.
4. Every table row still links to an official source; every unverified value still blank and flagged.
5. The disclosure bar and the no-testing/no-superlative rules are unchanged.

design.suggestion: Keep the layout a simple dashboard: sticky sidebar nav, top bar with disclosure, stat tiles, then tables
design.why: Familiar, scannable, loads fast on mobile.
design.path: Keep the current build.py chrome; tighten spacing and add one accent colour if anything changes.
design.status_note: Current build: sticky sidebar, sticky topbar, stat tiles on product pages, table-first content.

design.suggestion: Lead the landing page with a one-line value proposition, not a data table
design.why: Visitors decide in seconds whether to stay.
design.path: Hero band with the value proposition, then a format finder, then sourced article cards.
design.status_note: index.html ships the editorial hero ("Choose the shape before the model.") with hero actions and a format panel.

design.suggestion: Put the Amazon Associates + FTC disclosure above the fold on every page
design.why: Required by Amazon (Operating Agreement, S1) and the FTC (S7/S8/S9); it also builds trust.
design.path: Disclosure bar injected by layout() so no page can ship without it; link to compliance.html.
design.status_note: layout() injects the disclosure bar into every page; build guard check_disclosure fails the build if it is missing.

design.suggestion: Product cards: verified specs only; blank cells stay blank with a flagged pill; each row links to its official source
design.why: Transparency is the differentiator against AI slop sites that invent specs.
design.path: Reuse the existing table pattern; never fill a blank with a guess.
design.status_note: Product pages and data.html render blank cells as "not confirmed" with reason and flag link; check_rows_have_sources fails a value without a source.

design.suggestion: No product photos hotlinked from Amazon; use no photos or only brand-supplied assets
design.why: Amazon's IP licence (S2) restricts how Program Content may be used.
design.path: Spec-based cards instead of photo-led cards; link to the brand page instead of embedding.
design.status_note: Zero tags in the generated pages; the only images are the site's own assets (og-card.png is a meta tag, not page content).

design.suggestion: Comparison matrix: verified specs side by side, gaps visible, no price column
design.why: Program Policies restrict price display; showing gaps is honest and defensible.
design.path: compare.html stays a verified-only matrix with per-cell sources.
design.status_note: compare.html renders verified rows only; the category table's Amazon price column is blank by policy with S2 cited on the cell.

design.suggestion: Category subpages: one category index plus one page per product, with the category index growing as products are added
design.why: Gives search engines clear topical sections and internal-link paths.
design.path: categories/kitchen-appliances.html is the template; add one page per new category.
design.status_note: Implemented for the one category that exists (kitchen appliances, 3 products). New categories get no page until a product in them is tracked.

design.suggestion: Add JSON-LD (WebSite, Article, BreadcrumbList), Open Graph, Twitter card and meta descriptions to every page
design.why: Helps search engines understand the site and improves click-through from results and social shares.
design.path: Emit from build.py layout(); keep it static; guard it with a build check.
design.status_note: Shipped by pass 9 (PR #69) and extended by PR #74; enforced by build guard check_seo_metadata. Product/Offer/AggregateRating markup is deliberately not emitted because the site publishes no price or rating.

design.suggestion: Mobile-first: single-column stack below ~640px, readable touch targets, no horizontal scroll
design.why: Most affiliate traffic arrives on mobile.
design.path: Verify with device emulation before each release.
design.status_note: Breakpoints at 960/820/760/560px, a Menu toggle with aria-expanded, and prefers-reduced-motion support are in the shipped CSS/JS.

design.suggestion: Accessibility: colour contrast >= 4.5:1, focus-visible outlines, alt text, semantic headings
design.why: Legal good practice; excludes no readers.
design.path: Audit the CSS variables against WCAG AA once per quarter.
design.status_note: Skip link, :focus-visible outlines, semantic landmarks and reduced-motion support ship today; no scheduled contrast audit exists yet.

voice_rules.rule: One topic per page, and every page stamps when its sources were read
voice_rules.why: Focus for the reader, freshness signal for search engines, and an honest record of what the page is based on.

voice_rules.rule: Human voice: contractions, questions, specific numbers instead of 'very/really/incredible', short and long sentences mixed
voice_rules.why: The single fastest way to stop reading like generated filler. Specifics are also the only thing this site has - every number is sourced.

voice_rules.rule: Label vendor claims: anything the manufacturer says about its own product is marked a brand claim, not a tested fact
voice_rules.why: A repeated brand claim presented as an finding is the classic fake-review pattern; labelling it is both honest and compliant.

voice_rules.rule: Working titles are questions or decisions a reader types - never announcements like 'The Ultimate Guide to...'
voice_rules.why: Announcement titles are the loudest AI-slop tell, and they match no search query anyone types.
